skill.title: Draw and interpret nets of prisms, cylinders and cones

steps.title: Read the dimensions from the diagram

lines.text: A square of side $x$ is cut from each corner, so $x$ is removed from both ends of each 10-unit side.
The height is the folded-up side of a cut-out square.

steps.title: Count the corners and faces of a cube

lines.text: A cube has 8 corners and 6 faces, so $C = 8$ and $F = 6$.

steps.title: Check the identity
Convert each length using the scale 1 : 10

lines.text: Divide each length by 10. A scale of 1 : 10 turns 10 cm into 1 cm.
The box is 7 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high on the drawing. Each small square is 1 cm.

steps.title: Draw the net with six rectangles

lines.text: Draw a column 7 cm wide made of four rectangles, from top to bottom: $7 \times 2$, $7 \times 3$, $7 \times 2$, $7 \times 3$.
Add a $2 \times 3$ rectangle to each side of the second rectangle, to make the two ends of the box.

candidates.question:
A closed cylinder has radius $4$ cm and height $9$ cm.
When the curved surface is unrolled in its net, it forms a rectangle. Find the dimensions of this rectangle, correct to one decimal place.

steps.title: Find the height side of the rectangle

lines.text: The curved surface unrolls into a rectangle. One side is the height of the cylinder.

steps.title: Find the other side using the circumference

lines.text: The other side is the circumference of the circular base, $2\pi r$ with $r = 4$.

candidates.question:
A tin of beans is a cylinder with diameter $10$ cm and height $14$ cm.
The label goes once around the curved surface and is a rectangle in the net. Find the dimensions of the label, correct to one decimal place.

steps.title: Find the height side of the rectangle

lines.text: The label unrolls into a rectangle. One side is the height of the tin.

steps.title: Find the other side using the circumference

lines.text: The other side is the circumference of the circular base, $\pi d$ with $d = 10$.

steps.title: Find the height side of the rectangle

lines.text: An open cylinder unrolls into a rectangle. One side is the height of the cylinder.

steps.title: Find the other side using the circumference

lines.text: The other side is the circumference of the circular base, $2\pi r$ with $r = 5$.

steps.title: Complete the square to find the centre and radius

lines.text: Group the $x$ terms and the $y$ terms, then complete each square.

steps.title: Use the radius

lines.text: The right-hand side is $r^2$, and $r = 5\sqrt{3}$.

steps.title: Compare with the general circle equation

lines.text: The general form is $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$, with centre $(-g, -f)$ and radius $\sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}$.

Find the radius

skill.title: Decide whether circles touch internally or externally

steps.title: Find the line through the two centres

lines.text: Any circle touching $c$ externally at the same point as $s$ has its centre on the line through the centres of $c$ and $s$, beyond $s$.

steps.title: Pick a point on that line on the far side of s

lines.text: The touching point is $(4, 9)$, so the centre must have $x > 4$. Choose $x = 10$.

steps.title: Write circle c in centre-radius form

lines.text: Group the $x$ terms and the $y$ terms and move the constant across.
Complete the square: add $(4 \div 2)^2 = 4$ and $(2 \div 2)^2 = 1$ to both sides.

steps.title: Read off both centres and radii

lines.text: Circle $c$ has centre $(-2, 1)$ and radius $\sqrt{100} = 10$.
Circle $s$, $(x-7)^2 + (y-13)^2 = 25$, has centre $(7, 13)$ and radius $5$.

steps.title: Compare the sum of the radii with the distance between centres

lines.text: The distance between the centres equals $r_1 + r_2$, so the circles touch externally.

candidates.final: d = r_1 + r_2 = 15 \text{, so the circles touch externally}

steps.title: Read off circle c

lines.text: Circle $c$ is $(x-2)^2 + (y+1)^2 = 72$, so its centre is $(2, -1)$.

steps.title: Find the distance between the centres

lines.text: Centres: $(-2, 3)$ for $s$ and $(2, -1)$ for $c$.

steps.title: Find the difference between the radii
Conclude

lines.text: The distance between the centres equals the difference of the radii, so the circles touch internally.

candidates.question:
The circle $c_1$ has equation $x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 6y - 51 = 0$.
The circle $c_2$ has equation $x^2 + y^2 - 10x - 14y + 65 = 0$.
Show that $c_2$ touches $c_1$ internally.

steps.title: Write $c_1$ in centre-radius form

lines.text: Group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the square.
Centre $(2, 3)$, radius $\sqrt{64} = 8$.

steps.title: Write $c_2$ in centre-radius form

lines.text: Centre $(5, 7)$, radius $\sqrt{9} = 3$.

steps.title: Find the distance between the centres
Find the difference between the radii
Conclude

lines.text: The distance between the centres equals the difference of the radii, $d = r_1 - r_2 = 5$, so the circles touch internally.

candidates.final: d = r_1 - r_2 = 5 \text{, so the circles touch internally}

steps.title: Find the translation from the centre of s to the touching point

lines.text: The centres and the touching point are on one straight line, with the touching point between them.

steps.title: Halve it, since t has half the radius
Move from the touching point by this amount

lines.text: The centre of $t$ is this far from $(12, 11)$, continuing in the same direction.

skill.title: Test whether a point is on a line; find intercepts

steps.title: Read the point from the graph

lines.text: Read across to the $x$-value first, then up to the $y$-value. $F$ is 4 across and 1 up.

steps.title: Read each point from the grid

lines.text: Read across to the $x$-value, then up or down to the $y$-value. Write each as $(x, y)$.

steps.title: Read the co-ordinates of T

lines.text: In $(x, y) = (-2, -5)$, the first number is the $x$-value: $2$ units to the left of the origin.
The second number is the $y$-value: $5$ units down.
Mark the point where these meet and label it $T$.

steps.title: Substitute x = -2 and y = -5 into x - y - 3

lines.text: The left side equals $0$, so $T$ is on $k$.

steps.title: Pick a value for x and find y

lines.text: Choose $x = 1$ and put it into $x - y - 3 = 0$.

steps.title: Read each point off the grid

lines.text: Go across to the $x$ value first, then up or down to the $y$ value.
